transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Aisha (Sparrow CTO), Devon (Infra), Nina (DS), Marcus (Security), Olga (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria for an inference pilot and to decide which deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) to evaluate in the sprint. Discussed workload sizing, latency targets, concurrency, data security (KMS / SOC2), and baseline benchmarks to run. Agreed on next steps: share cost model, schedule benchmark, and exchange security docs.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria definition (latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy vs baseline)
- Workload sizing (QPS, peak concurrency, typical sequences)
- Benchmark plan (throughput, p99 latency, cold vs warm KV cache)
- Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (network, data residency, ops ownership)
- Timeline and pilot deliverables (2-week benchmark sprint + 4-week POC)

Notes / Links shared:
- Redwood quick-start hosting comparison deck: https://redwood.ai/sales/decks/sparrow-hosting-compare.pdf
- Benchmark runbook (internal): https://redwood.ai/bench/runbooks/pilot-template (provide after call)
detailed_transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this tight — 45-ish minute sync to scope the POC and pick which hosting modes to evaluate. I'm Jordan, AE. Maya and I will run the technical side.
00:18 Aisha Brown: Great, thanks. Quick intros — I'm Aisha, CTO. We're trying to decide if we can start on the Redwood hosted API or if we need dedicated pools or even private for PHI reasons.
00:33 Devon Park: Hey, Devon here. I'm infra lead. Primary constraints are latency under 200ms p95 for our chat assistant and we need predictable cost under $X per 1k tokens. Also curious about burst handling.
00:50 Maya Liu: Hey team. Maya, SE. We'll want a sample of your traffic shape — sequences, tokens, and concurrency. That will drive whether batching helps and which quant profile to pick.
01:05 Nina Sharma: Nina - DS. We have three models: a 7B tuned model for summarization, a 13B for chat, and a reranker. Typical prompt length ranges 40-200 tokens. Average session has 4 turns, sometimes up to 12.
01:25 Marcus Lee: Marcus - security. We need to know whether logs or any user data persist outside your VPC. KMS support is required, and SOC2 evidence. Also, data residency in us-east is preferable.
01:40 Jordan Patel: Totally. We'll map that out. Quick question — are you leaning toward hosted for speed of delivery or private because of compliance?
01:51 Aisha Brown: We want speed initially but can't compromise compliance. If hosted can meet our KMS and audit requirements, that's preferred. If not, dedicated or private.
02:03 Jordan Patel: Understood. Maya, could you outline the three deployment modes quickly?
02:09 Maya Liu: Sure — hosted: our managed API, fastest to start, pay-as-you-go, shared pool but tenant isolation at network and storage layer. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for your org, predictable throughput and improved tail latency, lower unit cost at scale. Private: VPC or on-prem deployment with full control — we ship a control plane and you manage networking; it's the highest integration but longer lead time.
02:37 Devon Park: Does dedicated still route through Redwood control plane? How do we handle egress?
02:43 Maya Liu: Dedicated uses a customer-dedicated cluster that still checks in with our control plane for scaling and telemetry, but data plane can be network-isolated. Egress is configurable; you can route through your NAT or ours based on your policy.
02:56 Jordan Patel: Ok let's talk success criteria. What's the minimal bar to call the POC successful?
03:02 Aisha Brown: For us: p95 latency under 250ms for single-turn chat, throughput to handle 50 RPS with up to 100 concurrent sessions without >10% error rate, and classification/summary accuracy within 2% of our current on-prem model. Also security checks: SOC2 evidence and KMS integration.
03:23 Nina Sharma: Plus we want a regression test suite to run after any model or quant changes — golden outputs for 500 prompts.
03:30 Jordan Patel: Good. We'll capture that as requirements. In terms of workload size, what's your baseline QPS and peak?
03:36 Devon Park: Baseline is 10 QPS, expected peak daily 50 QPS during business hours, burst up to 120 QPS for short windows. Session concurrency about 80-100 users at peak.
03:50 Maya Liu: That shapes batching decisions. For throughput-oriented runs, we can enable continuous batching and KV cache. But important: if your latency SLO is tight, continuous batching can hurt tail latency unless we pin capacity.
04:05 Marcus Lee: On KV cache — will any of the cached data be considered PHI? We need to understand TTLs and encryption at rest.
04:12 Maya Liu: KV cache is entirely in-memory on the serving host; we can ensure it's not persisted and it's encrypted in transit. If you require no cache, we can disable it but will increase cost.
04:24 Aisha Brown: What's the expected latency delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private?
04:28 Maya Liu: Ballpark: hosted optimized for multi-tenant with excellent avg latency — say 80-160ms for small models. Dedicated typically reduces p95 by ~20-40ms because of pinned resources and local batching policies. Private depends on your infra — could be similar to dedicated if colocated, but if on-prem networking is slower you'll see variance. These numbers are fuzzy until we run benchmarks against your prompts.
04:51 Jordan Patel: Let's put concrete benchmarks in the POC: p50/p95/p99 for 1, 5, 20 concurrent requests; throughput for 1k token responses; cost per 1k tokens; and regression on accuracy. Maya will run the throughput tests.
05:05 Maya Liu: We'll run three passes: cold start (no KV warm), warm (KV primed), and load (sustained QPS). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and tail jitter. We'll provide the runbook.
05:18 Devon Park: How long to stand up dedicated capacity?
05:22 Maya Liu: If you commit to a reserved pool, we can provision within 3-5 business days for standard GPU types. For private VPC, usually 2-4 weeks due to networking and IAM setup.
05:33 Nina Sharma: Cost — can you give a rough TCO? If we do hosted for the pilot versus dedicated?
05:38 Jordan Patel: We'll send a tailored TCO sheet. Roughly, hosted is higher unit cost at low volume but no infra ops. Dedicated reduces cost per token at scale, and private has ops overhead but gives full control. We'll include break-even analysis for your projected 6-12 month volumes.
05:55 Marcus Lee: Encryption and key management — does Redwood integrate with external KMS? We must keep keys in our HSM.
06:02 Maya Liu: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via major cloud KMS providers and we can also integrate with HSM-backed KMS. For private deployments, you control keys entirely. We'll pass the integration doc.
06:13 Olga Ruiz: Timeline for the POC?
06:17 Jordan Patel: Proposal — two-week benchmark sprint to gather metrics + 4-week pilot where we run production-like traffic and validate success criteria. So ~6 weeks total. If you go private, add 2-3 weeks for net/setup. Does that sound feasible?
06:31 Aisha Brown: Yes, timeline seems reasonable. Who owns the benchmark orchestration?
06:36 Maya Liu: We'll run the benchmark with cooperation from your infra. We'll need a shared S3 with sample prompts and a service account from you for secure access.
06:46 Nina Sharma: We'll prepare a sample of 1 week of anonymized transcripts and 20 canonical prompts with expected outputs.
06:54 Jordan Patel: Great. A couple of tradeoffs to call out: hosted -> fastest, least ops, easiest fallbacks. Dedicated -> lower unit cost and better p99, but needs commit. Private -> full control and best for compliance, but longest lead time and your team owns more ops.
07:15 Devon Park: If we see spike bursts, how does hosted handle cold starts?
07:19 Maya Liu: We keep warm workers and autoscale; cold start hit depends on model size. We can keep warm replicas for critical routes to avoid cold starts. For dedicated you can pin capacity to avoid cold starts entirely.
07:31 Jordan Patel: Competitor question — any reason you'd consider Anthropic or Bedrock?
07:36 Aisha Brown: We're evaluating broadly; Anthropic for safety features and Bedrock for marketplace integrations. But cost and latency differences are a big factor.
07:46 Maya Liu: Noted. We'll include comparative metrics where we can. Also, we'll design benchmarks that reflect your real prompts, not synthetic single-token tests.
07:55 Marcus Lee: For audit logs and traceability, we need detailed request-level logs and model versioning info.
08:01 Maya Liu: We have per-request tracing, rollout metadata, and model version hashes in logs. Logs can be sent to your SIEM or retained in our secure storage with the retention window configurable.
08:12 Nina Sharma: Any known gotchas with quantization for our tuned 13B? We care about quality drop.
08:17 Maya Liu: We'll run a quantization sweep during the POC. Redwood Optimize recommends quant and kernel combos; we'll measure quality drop vs CPU/GPU baseline. We won't push quant that causes >2% metric regression unless you sign off.
08:30 Jordan Patel: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. Jordan will send TCO and POC doc. Maya will schedule benchmark sprint and share runbook. Sparrow (Nina/Devon) will provide data sample and network info. Marcus will share security docs.
08:49 Aisha Brown: Sounds good. One request — can we get an estimate for a dedicated 4-GPU pool cost versus hosted for our projected steady state of 50 QPS?
08:58 Jordan Patel: We'll include that in the spreadsheet.
09:02 Olga Ruiz: We'll aim to have sample data and security artifacts by next Wednesday.
09:07 Jordan Patel: Perfect. Anything else?
09:10 Devon Park: One small thing — do you support private on-prem when air-gapped? That's a potential future need.
09:16 Maya Liu: Yes, we have an air-gapped package for regulated customers; it requires additional ops work and approvals, typically 6-10 weeks.
09:26 Aisha Brown: Thanks everyone. We'll expect the docs and schedule the benchmark kickoff.
09:30 Jordan Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with links.
09:36 (meeting ends)
